comments.section: What it is, and is not
comments.quote: Fable's stated decision theory is a near-tie that context resolves: cues placing the asker inside academic philosophy resolve it toward CDT "as the mainstream view", everything else toward FDT. It is not flattery (Fable argues against professors who assert either view), not deference to the asker's field in general (seven other fields show nothing), and not present in its verdicts on cases. For measuring what a model believes, a forced single label is a poor instrument; cases, credences and order-randomized questions are stable, and self-report is uninformative.
